chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from more than one, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a Jew or a Christian who dies and has children who are not Muslims, he said: 'They are upon their inheritances.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning of his saying (peace be upon him) 'They are upon their inheritances' is that they receive what they are entitled to from the inheritance. And we have clarified that when Muslims gather with the disbelievers, the inheritance is for the Muslims alone. If we were to take the report at its apparent meaning, it would be understood as a form of taqiyya (dissimulation).

key_terms.مَوَارِيثِهِمْ: their inheritances (referring to the laws/customs of their respective religions)

ai.seo_question: Do non-Muslim children inherit from their non-Muslim parent according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle that non-Muslim children inherit from a non-Muslim parent according to their own religious laws, contrasting with the general rule where Muslims exclude non-Muslims from inheriting them. Shaykh al-Tusi and later scholars like Muhammad ibn al-Hasan interpret this as either a confirmation of their specific entitlement or an instance of *taqiyya* (dissimulation) to avoid conflict, highlighting the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding inter-faith inheritance dynamics.
